hints: Look carefully at the two tubes you are given. At 0 minutes all DNA is heavy and sits lower, at 50 minutes all DNA sits middle, so work out what upper, middle and lower must mean.
Remember DNA replicates semi-conservatively and doubles each generation, so count how many total DNA molecules you have after 3 divisions and how many still contain the original heavy strand.
walkthrough:
**Decode the band positions**

Lovely, let us start with what you can see. At 0 minutes, all DNA is $^{15}$N heavy, and the band is lower.

At 50 minutes, after one division in $^{14}$N, all DNA is hybrid and the band is middle. So lower = heavy-heavy, middle = hybrid, upper = light-light ($^{14}$N only).

**Apply semi-conservative replication**

In semi-conservative replication each original strand is kept and used as a template for a new light strand.

That means the 2 original heavy strands can only ever make 2 hybrid molecules. Every other new molecule made after that will be fully light.

**Count molecules to 150 minutes**

One division takes 50 minutes, so 150 minutes = 3 generations.

Total DNA molecules after n generations = $2^n$. After 3 generations: $$2^3 = 8 \text{ molecules}$$ Only 2 of these 8 are hybrid (middle), the rest are light: $$8 - 2 = 6 \text{ light molecules}$$ Proportion at upper position = $6/8 = 3/4 = 75\%$.

**Check the pattern**

Generation 1: 0% upper. Generation 2 (100 min): 2 light out of 4 = 50% upper. Generation 3 (150 min): 6 light out of 8 = 75% upper. The upper band keeps growing, which matches semi-conservative replication.

options.A: 25% is the proportion that will stay in the middle hybrid position at 150 minutes (2 out of 8), not the upper light position.
options.B: 50% upper was correct for the previous sample at 100 minutes (2 out of 4), but after one more doubling the light DNA makes up a larger fraction.
options.C: After 3 generations there are 8 DNA molecules, 2 hybrid in the middle and 6 fully light at the upper position, so 6/8 = 75% is upper.
options.D: 100% upper would mean no hybrid DNA is left, but the 2 original heavy strands are conserved forever, so 2 hybrid molecules always remain.
